desc:
There are n unknown integers v0 .. vn-1. Each entry [a, b, d] of constraints states that va - vb = d (d may be negative or zero). Return true if values exist that satisfy every constraint simultaneously, otherwise false. Unmentioned variables are free. Note that a may equal b.

n = 3, constraints = [[0,1,2],[1,2,3],[0,2,5]]   -> true   (v0 = v1+2 = v2+5)
n = 3, constraints = [[0,1,2],[1,2,3],[0,2,4]]   -> false  (the first two force v0 - v2 = 5)
n = 2, constraints = [[1,1,0]]                    -> true
n = 2, constraints = [[1,1,3]]                    -> false  (v1 - v1 is always 0)
constraints: constraints[i] = [a, b, d] with 0 ≤ a, b < n and -10<sup>9</sup> ≤ d ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>
hints: Each constraint relates two variables by a fixed offset. Variables connected through constraints form groups in which all values are determined relative to one another.
Keep, for every variable, its offset from the root of its group (offset[x] = vx - vroot). Then va - vb = offset[a] - offset[b] if both have the same root.

Process constraints one by one with a weighted union-find. Same root: compare offset[a] - offset[b] with d. Different roots: attach one root under the other with the offset d - offset[a] + offset[b]. Update offsets during path compression.
editorial: This is union-find with potentials. diff[x] stores vx - vparent(x); find(x) returns the root and, while compressing the path, replaces diff[x] by the offset to the root (accumulate the diffs along the path from the root downwards). Then the relation between any two variables of the same group is known.

For a constraint [a, b, d] with roots ra, rb: if ra == rb the constraint is consistent only if diff[a] - diff[b] == d. Otherwise set parent[ra] = rb and diff[ra] = d - diff[a] + diff[b], which is exactly what makes va - vb = d true. Once every constraint passed, the groups can be shifted freely, so a solution exists. Time O((n + m) log n) amortised with path compression alone, and nearly linear when you also union by size. A BFS that assigns values along edges gives the same answer.
